_doc: SPLIT-LANE validation of the storage-layout hypothesis from wal-decomp-lane0: with WAL shards on dedicated NVMe lanes AND stream files on their own separate NVMe lane, wal+syncfs-checkpoint should reach ~250k ops/s FLAT across 10k->100k streams (ref-3s hit 270k @10k when WAL had dedicated lanes, ~= the 260k nofsync machinery ceiling; the old 8-18k @100k collapse was streams sitting on the PD boot disk). Layout via gke/durable-streams-splitlane.yaml (SPLITLANE=1): device 0 = /data/wal/0 (data root: streams/, the checkpoint syncfs domain), devices 1-5 = /data/wal/0/wal/<0..4> (5 WAL shard lanes). All arms: --data-dir /data/wal/0 --wal-shards 5. Arms: ref-3s (syncfs @3s = production candidate), ckpt-off (checkpoint deferred 1h — isolates commit-fsync cost on this layout), nofsync (machinery ceiling control). Success = ref-3s ~= ckpt-off ~= nofsync at BOTH stream counts, proving checkpoint + commit fsync are both ~free on the right layout. Requires SPLITLANE=1 SERVER_LOCAL_SSD_BLOCK=1 SPOT_SERVER=1 IMG_SERVER=...:ckptoff (image has --wal-checkpoint-interval-ms + --unsafe-disable-fsync).
